subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening

question: Should Gateway fetch-metadata and forwarded-header contradiction checks be an opt-in strict policy layered onto the existing origin allowlist, or a new default-on pre-upgrade security boundary that can reject otherwise allowed browser clients?
rationale: This choice changes the Gateway's browser and reverse-proxy compatibility contract, adds public configuration, and determines whether the existing origin allowlist remains authoritative; code review cannot safely choose that product security policy.

options.title: Preserve canonical allowlist policy
options.body: Refactor the checks into the existing upgrade owner, reuse current config and proxy helpers, and make the additional strict rejections opt-in with upgrade coverage.

options.title: Adopt a strict default
options.body: Keep default-on rejection only with explicit maintainer approval, consolidated configuration, public migration guidance, security-audit integration, and proof for legitimate cross-site WebView and proxy deployments.

options.title: Pause for policy consolidation
options.body: Defer this PR until the related origin-pattern work establishes one shared pre-upgrade browser-origin and fetch-metadata contract.

recommendation.title: Preserve canonical allowlist policy
recommendation.body: Refactor the checks into the existing upgrade owner, reuse current config and proxy helpers, and make the additional strict rejections opt-in with upgrade coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR explicitly requests this person's decision on the Gateway origin/security boundary and coordination with the related allowlist work.
